newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Gingrich, UN boss, top Russians due at Swiss forum.
newsitem.headline: Gingrich, UN boss, top Russians due at Swiss forum.

text.p: Controversial U.S. politician Newt Gingrich will rub shoulders at this year's Davos World Economic Forum with new United Nations Secretary-General Kofi Annan and top Russian leaders, the organisers indicated on Thursday.

Also at the gathering of top world political and business figures in the Swiss mountain resort from January 30 to February 4 will be presidents and prime ministers from former European communist countries and Asia.

This year's theme for the week-long meeting is "Building the Network Society", but participants will also address the effect of the growing integration of the world economy on the job market in the richer countries where unemployment is high.
Labour union leaders from Europe, the United States, Asia and South Africa will take part in this discussion.

To lead a debate on the European single currency will be European Commission President Jacques Santer, British Chancellor of the Exchequer Kenneth Clarke, German Finance Minister Theodor Waigel and Bank of France Governor Jean-Claude Trichet.
Officials at the Geneva-based foundation which has staged the Davos meeting since 1971 made clear they were delighted at getting an acceptance from Gingrich.

The Republican speaker of the House of Representatives, only narrowly re-elected this month after a funding scandal, will be the most senior U.S. political figure to attend for many years, although top U.S. business executives regularly go.
Three years ago, President Bill Clinton addressed the gathering by satellite, and Forum officials said they were hoping that Vice-President Al Gore might accept an invitation to attend this time.

From Russia, Prime Minister Viktor Chernomyrdin and Anatoly Chubais, chief of staff to President Boris Yeltsin, both regular stars in the Davos firmament, have said they will come, according to the Forum.

The gathering, brainchild of German academic Klaus Schwab, has grown rapidly from modest beginnings to become a key event on the world business and political calendar, attracting would-be as well as current leaders.
Many opposition politicians have used it to build up their contacts with officials and business and financial figures from other countries and to win the international media exposure Davos offers.

Forum officials said an invitation to attend this year had been extended to Tony Blair, leader of Britain's Labour Party which opinion polls suggest will oust the present Conservative government in elections due in May.
But Labour Party officials had yet to give a formal response, the officials added.
Also from the United States will be Deputy Treasury Secretary Lawrence Summers, as well as Bill Gates, chief executive of software giant Microsoft and John Smith, General Motors chairman.

Among top participants from Asia will be India's Prime Minister H.D. Deve Gowda, Cambodia's First Prime Minister Prince Norodom Ranariddh, Mongolia's Prime Minister Mendsaikhany Enkhsaikhan, and Singapore's Deputy Prime Minister and Defence Minister Tony Tan Keng Yam.

Attending from the former Soviet-bloc countries will be Prime Minister Vaclav Klaus of the Czech Republic, new Romanian President Emil Constantinescu, President Aleksander Kwasniewski of Poland and President Arpad Goencz of Hungary.
